mission: Mission 1 - source discovery, acquisition and corpus infrastructure
note: Registry of every channel investigated, including the ones rejected. Candidate counts live in stats.json because they change as collection resumes; this file records attributes that do not.

sources.name: GitHub Code Search API (authenticated)
sources.access_method: gh api (stored OAuth keyring credential); one page of 100 hits per query; 42 workflow queries; 7 s pause between calls (authenticated limit is 10 requests/minute)
sources.license: per-file: none declared by the API; repository licence resolved via GET /repos/{owner}/{repo} and recorded per sample
sources.redistribution: Manifest row only (hash, path, URL, licence). File bytes stay in a local cache outside Git, so no redistribution question arises.
sources.size: 864,256 hits measured for a single broad query; 100 hits/query/page sampled
limitations: Code Search returns at most 1000 files per query and ranks by relevance, so a single broad query is a biased sample of a very large population.
Same notebook is mirrored across tutorial repos; exact and code-level dedup are mandatory.
Repository licence is a repository-level signal and can be wrong per file (vendored code, third-party snippets).
raw.githubusercontent.com HEAD is the default branch, which can move; the recorded commit_sha pins the manifest to the state observed at collection time.

sources.name: Curated public ML repositories (whole-tree enumeration)
sources.access_method: gh api GET /repos/{r} (licence, default branch), GET /repos/{r}/commits/{branch} (immutable commit), GET /repos/{r}/git/trees/{branch}?recursive=1 (paths and sizes), then raw.githubusercontent.com per file
sources.license: per repository, recorded per sample (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, Unlicense in this run; 78 of the 262 samples came from repositories that declare no licence or NOASSERTION)
sources.redistribution: Manifest row only; bytes stay in the out-of-Git cache. Samples under copyleft licences are marked not redistributable.
sources.size: 39 curated repositories, tree listing per repository, at most 8 files kept per repository
limitations: Teaching repositories are cleaned-up and leakage is rarer than in competition or personal notebooks, which biases the channel toward legitimate code.
An 8-file-per-repository cap trades volume for repository diversity.
Path-order selection takes the alphabetically first notebooks, not the most interesting ones.
Translated copies (translations/, i18n/) are skipped by path filter; residual mirrors are caught by dedup.

sources.name: DistilKaggle notebook corpus (Zenodo)
sources.access_method: HTTP byte-range requests against https://zenodo.org/api/records/10317389/files/code.csv/content (3,855,164,281 bytes); 36 evenly spaced 1.2 MB ranges; rows regrouped by kernel_id into reconstructed notebooks
sources.license: CC-BY-4.0 (record metadata); the upstream Kaggle notebook code may carry its own terms
sources.redistribution: Attribution-only per CC-BY-4.0, but the reconstructed notebooks are still kept in the local cache rather than committed, to avoid asserting rights over third-party kernels.
sources.size: 3855 MB code.csv; 1423 MB markdown.csv; 1531 MB DistilKaggle.tar.gz; 515 MB kernel_metrics.csv; 52.8 MB kernels.tar.gz; ~517k notebooks in total
limitations: code.csv is kernel-contiguous and ordered by kernel_id, so byte-range sampling is a spread over the id space, not a random sample of the corpus.
Outputs, markdown and notebook metadata are not in code.csv: the reconstruction is code cells only, so cell-level evidence is approximate.
Throughput was measured at 0.8-1.2 MB/s, so the whole file (about 50 min) is out of scope; only ~43 MB was transferred.
Kaggle kernels are heavily duplicated (forked and re-published), so the near-duplicate rate is expected to be high.
No per-kernel licence is available in code.csv; the CC-BY-4.0 record licence is the only licence signal.

sources.name: Kaggle public API / public notebooks
sources.license: per-kernel, often unspecified; Kaggle terms restrict scraping and redistribution
limitations: Requires an authenticated Kaggle account and acceptance of competition-specific rules.
Terms of service restrict bulk download and redistribution, so it is not used as a channel in this mission.

sources.name: HuggingFace jupyter-agent/kaggle-notebooks-edu-v0
sources.license: no licence tag on the dataset card
limitations: No licence metadata, so neither analysis nor redistribution can be justified from the dataset card alone.
Content is a Kaggle-derived mirror, so it would duplicate the DistilKaggle channel rather than add independent repositories.

sources.name: HuggingFace bigcomputer/meta-kaggle-notebook
sources.license: no licence tag on the dataset card
limitations: Metadata only (titles, votes, tags): no notebook source, so it cannot contribute code samples.
Would be useful for prioritising kernels if a licensed source for their code existed.

sources.name: HuggingFace lvwerra/jupyter-notebooks-edu-v0..v4, codeShare/JupyterNotebooks
sources.license: no licence tag on the dataset cards
limitations: No licence metadata.
Largely GitHub-derived, so the same repositories already reached directly through the GitHub channels; adding them would inflate counts without adding independent repositories.
A candidate for a future mission if per-file licences can be resolved.

sources.name: Phase 6 frozen real-world holdout
sources.access_method: reference only; never touched by this mission
sources.license: per repository, recorded in the corpus module
sources.redistribution: unchanged from the original corpus decision
limitations: Frozen: must not be modified, re-tuned against, or combined with new candidates.
New expansion samples are hashed against the frozen 60-notebook directory and flagged overlaps_frozen=true so contamination is visible.
